formation.title: The Romanian Kingdom
formation.text:
The three lands of the Romanians (Wallachia, Moldavia, and Transylvania) are united under a single crown at last. For centuries, the Romanian people endured as subjects divided between Ottoman vassalage, Habsburg domination, and precarious independence. Now, from Bucharest, the new kingdom looks upon its Carpathian heartland and the fertile Danubian plain with the question that has defined every Romanian ruler since Basarab: shall we be the shield that holds the line, or the crossroads that grows rich from all who pass?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are the bulwark: Christendom's last fortress.

modifiers.name: Antemurale Christianitatis
modifiers.text: Romania stands as the bulwark of Christendom against the Ottoman tide, a fortress-nation whose mountains and rivers form a natural shield for all of Europe.

options.text: We are the crossroads: the Danube's richest realm.

modifiers.name: Danubian Prosperity
modifiers.text: Seated at the crossroads of three empires, Romania harnesses the wealth of the Danube (its grain, its livestock, its salt) to build a prosperous and cultured kingdom.

advances.name: Voivodal Tradition
advances.text: The system of the voivode, war-chief and prince, anchors Romanian governance in both martial authority and landholding custom.

advances.name: Legacy of Posada
advances.text: At the Battle of Posada in 1330, Basarab I ambushed and destroyed a vastly superior Hungarian army in a mountain pass, establishing Wallachian independence through cavalry skill and knowledge of the terrain.

advances.name: Carpathian Salt Wealth
advances.text: The vast salt deposits of the Carpathians have been worked since antiquity, providing the Romanian principalities with a reliable source of wealth and a crucial trade commodity.

advances.name: Mountain Fortresses
advances.text: From Poenari to Bran, fortresses guarding the Carpathian passes form the backbone of Romanian defense against invaders from every direction.

advances.name: Orthodox Foundation
advances.text: The establishment of Orthodox metropolitan sees in Wallachia and Moldavia gave the principalities spiritual independence to match their political autonomy.

advances.name: Boyar Estates
advances.text: The boyar landowning class formed the backbone of Romanian governance, administering justice and collecting revenues across the principalities.

advances.name: Fortified Churches
advances.text: Over 150 fortified churches in Transylvania served as both places of worship and community refuges against Tatar, Ottoman, and other raiders.

advances.name: Danubian Trade
advances.text: The Danube and its tributaries carried Romanian grain, salt, livestock, and hides to markets across central Europe and the Black Sea.

advances.name: Order of the Dragon
advances.text: Vlad Tepes employed terror as a weapon of state, impalement, scorched earth, and the night attack at Targoviste demonstrated that an outnumbered defender could break the will of a larger invader.

advances.name: Athleta Christi
advances.text: Stephen the Great of Moldavia won 46 of his 48 battles, earning the title 'Champion of Christ' from Pope Sixtus IV for his defense of Christendom at the Battle of Vaslui.

advances.name: Painted Monasteries
advances.text: After each victory, Stephen the Great founded a monastery. His successors covered their walls with breathtaking frescoes, creating the Painted Monasteries of Bukovina.

event.title: The Painted Monasteries
event.text: In the hills of Moldavia, the monasteries built by Stephen the Great and his successors have been transformed into something unprecedented. Their exterior walls blaze with frescoes depicting saints, biblical scenes, and the siege of Constantinople, entire theological libraries painted for an illiterate congregation to read. At Voronet, the particular shade of blue used by the painters has become famous across the Orthodox world, a color that defies reproduction. At Humor, Moldovita, and Sucevita, the same tradition continues. These are not merely churches but declarations of faith in pigment and plaster, built to endure against weather and conquest alike. Pope Sixtus IV once named Stephen 'Athleta Christi', and these monasteries are his enduring testament.

options.text: A legacy in paint and stone.

modifiers.name: Legacy of the Painted Monasteries
modifiers.text: The painted monasteries of Moldavia stand as monuments to Orthodox devotion and artistic genius, inspiring cultural pride across the united principalities.

advances.name: Princely Authority
advances.text: The consolidation of voivodal power over the boyar council strengthened central governance across the Romanian principalities.

advances.name: Pastoral Wealth
advances.text: Romanian wool, hides, and livestock were exported in vast quantities to Transylvania, Poland, and the Ottoman Empire, forming the economic backbone of the principalities.

advances.name: Lefegii Tradition
advances.text: Professional mercenary infantry, the Lefegii, supplemented the feudal levies of the principalities, providing experienced border troops skilled in mountain warfare.

advances.name: Calarasi Tradition
advances.text: The Calarasi were Wallachian frontier cavalry, mounted scouts and patrol riders who guarded the borders and carried dispatches across the vast Danubian plain.

advances.name: Scorched Earth Doctrine
advances.text: Romanian defenders systematically denied resources to invaders, poisoning wells, diverting rivers, and retreating into the mountains to wear down superior forces through attrition.

advances.name: Curtea de Arges
advances.text: The monastery at Curtea de Arges, built by Neagoe Basarab in 1517, represents the pinnacle of Romanian ecclesiastical architecture and scholarly patronage.

advances.name: Danubian Grain Trade
advances.text: The fertile Danubian plain and Wallachian lowlands produced wheat surpluses and livestock hides that fed and clothed markets from Constantinople to central Europe.

advances.name: Chancellery Reform
advances.text: The modernization of princely chancelleries introduced systematic record-keeping and administrative procedures modeled on Byzantine and Polish practices.

advances.name: First Unification
advances.text: In 1600, Michael the Brave briefly united Wallachia, Transylvania, and Moldavia, the first time all three Romanian lands were ruled by one prince.

event.title: The First Unification
event.text: In 1600, Michael the Brave accomplished what no Romanian ruler had done before. He united Wallachia, Transylvania, and Moldavia under a single crown. After routing the Ottomans at Calugareni with barely 16,000 men against Sinan Pasha's force, he turned north. At Selimbar, he defeated the Transylvanian prince Andreas Bathory. By May 1600, his armies had taken Moldavia as well. For one brief, shining moment, the three Romanian lands were one. But the Habsburgs and Poles would not tolerate such unity. Within a year, Michael was betrayed and assassinated at Campia Turzii. The union dissolved as quickly as it had been forged. Now, centuries later, the dream lives again. The question is what to do with it.

options.text: Press forward: finish what Michael began.

modifiers.name: Press the Advantage
modifiers.text: In the spirit of Michael the Brave, Romania's armies push forward to claim what belongs to the Romanian people by right of blood and sword.

modifiers.name: Consolidate the Realm
modifiers.text: Rather than overextend as Michael once did, Romania secures its hold over the three principalities, binding them through law and common purpose.

advances.name: Confessional Resilience
advances.text: While Transylvania became a battleground of Reformation and Counter-Reformation, Romanian Orthodoxy persisted as a unifying cultural force across all three principalities.

advances.name: Reform of the Host
advances.text: The transformation of the Oastea from a feudal levy into a more professional force, with paid soldiers and standardized equipment replacing the old boyar retinues.

advances.name: Seimeni Guards
advances.text: The Seimeni were professional guards recruited by Moldavian and Wallachian princes, standing infantry paid in cash and land, forming a reliable core around which the feudal host was organized.

advances.name: Transylvanian Mines
advances.text: The silver and copper mines of Transylvania, particularly around Baia Mare and Rosia Montana, provided mineral wealth that attracted Saxon settlers and fueled regional trade.

advances.name: The Pravila
advances.text: The codification of customary law in written legal codes, the Pravilele, brought consistency to governance across the principalities, replacing oral tradition with written statute.

advances.name: Cultural Awakening
advances.text: The emergence of Romanian-language literature, chronicles, and religious texts fostered a shared identity among Romanians across the three principalities.

advances.name: Phanariote Reform
advances.text: Though the Phanariote era brought Greek-speaking governors from Constantinople, it also introduced administrative reforms, legal codification, and connections to Enlightenment ideas.

advances.name: Rosiori Tradition
advances.text: The Rosiori, 'Red Ones', were Romania's light cavalry elite, distinguished by their red uniforms and skill in reconnaissance, raiding, and pursuit.

advances.name: Vanatori de Munte
advances.text: The Vanatori, Romanian mountain hunters, were light infantry specialists trained in the Carpathian highlands, expert at ambush, alpine warfare, and independent operations in rough terrain.

advances.name: Organic Statute
advances.text: The Regulamentul Organic of 1831-32 established a modern constitutional framework for the Danubian Principalities, reforming taxation, justice, and public administration.

advances.name: Breadbasket of the East
advances.text: Romania's vast wheat production made it the granary of southeastern Europe, with grain exports flowing through Braila and Galati to markets across the Mediterranean.

advances.name: Border Modernization
advances.text: The modernization of Romania's border defenses replaced medieval fortresses with modern fortifications adapted to artillery warfare.

advances.name: War of Independence
advances.text: At Plevna, Grivitsa, and Rahova in 1877-78, Romanian soldiers fought alongside Russian forces to win full independence from Ottoman suzerainty.

event.title: The War of Independence
event.text: At Plevna, Grivitsa, and Rahova, Romanian soldiers have proven that this nation can stand among the powers of Europe. The Dorobanti, peasant soldiers drawn from every village of the kingdom, held the line against Ottoman regulars and earned Romania's independence with blood and courage. The great powers that once treated the Danubian Principalities as pawns must now reckon with a sovereign kingdom. On May 9, 1877, the Romanian parliament declared full independence, and the army crossed the Danube to make that declaration real. The Kingdom of Romania stands recognized by the Treaty of Berlin, no longer a vassal, no longer a pawn, but a nation in its own right.

advances.name: National Awakening
advances.text: The Transylvanian School and subsequent intellectual movements standardized the Romanian language, revived Latin-alphabet writing, and forged a modern national consciousness.

advances.name: Cuza's Reforms
advances.text: Alexandru Ioan Cuza's sweeping reforms (land redistribution, secularization of monasteries, universal education) transformed Romania from a feudal society into a modern state.

advances.name: Oil Industry
advances.text: Romania was among the world's first oil producers, with refineries at Ploiesti operational from the 1850s. By 1900, Romania was Europe's largest petroleum exporter.

advances.name: Paris of the East
advances.text: Bucharest's transformation into a cosmopolitan capital (with French-inspired boulevards, neo-classical architecture, and thriving intellectual salons) earned it the epithet 'Micul Paris.'

advances.name: Modern Romanian Army
advances.text: The reorganization of the Romanian army along Prussian lines, with modern equipment, officer academies, and conscription, created a capable national force.

destiny.name: Destiny of Romania
destiny.text: United at last, the Romanian kingdom must now choose its path. Will it be the shield that guards Christendom or the crossroads that grows rich from all who pass?

event.title: The Destiny of Romania
event.text: The three lands are united, the crown secured, and the realm at peace, for the moment. But Romania sits at the crossroads of empires, and peace is never more than a generation away from the next storm. The Carpathians shelter us, the Danube feeds us, and the Orthodox faith sustains us. Now the question is not whether Romania will endure, but what it will become. The destiny of the Romanian people is ours to forge.

destiny.name: Fortress of the Danube
destiny.text: The Danubian fortresses of Vidin and Nikopol must be wrested from Ottoman hands to secure Romania's southern frontier and establish its claim as defender of the Christian world.

event.title: Fortress of the Danube
event.text: The fortresses of Vidin and Nikopol, once the staging grounds for Ottoman campaigns into the heart of Europe, now fly the Romanian standard. These ancient strongholds on the Danube's south bank have been the gateway through which invasion after invasion poured into the Balkans. No longer. Romanian garrisons now man the walls that generations of Christian kingdoms failed to hold. The Danubian line is ours, and with it, the first proof that Romania can be more than a buffer state. It can be a bulwark.

destiny.name: Crushing the Crescent
destiny.text: With the Danubian line secured, the campaign must press deeper into Ottoman territory. Take Edirne, the old Ottoman capital in Europe, and prove that the tide has turned.

event.title: Crushing the Crescent
event.text: Edirne has fallen. The city that served as the Ottoman capital before Constantinople, where Murad I built his first European palace and from which the sultans launched their conquests of the Balkans, is now in Romanian hands. The symbolism is unmistakable, the tide of Ottoman power in Europe has been broken not by a coalition of great powers but by the nation that suffered most under it. Our armies stand deep in Thrace, and the question before us is how to press this advantage.

options.text: Storm every wall: give them no rest.

modifiers.name: Storm the Walls
modifiers.text: Romania's armies press every siege with furious aggression, storming fortifications rather than waiting for starvation to do its work.

options.text: Hold our ground: let time do its work.

modifiers.name: Hold the Line
modifiers.text: Romania fights the long war, maintaining its armies cheaply, replacing losses steadily, and wearing down the enemy through patience and endurance.

destiny.name: Restorer of Christendom
destiny.text: The ultimate prize: Constantinople itself. Take the city that fell in 1453 and restore it to Christian hands. Romania's destiny as Antemurale Christianitatis will be fulfilled.

event.title: Restorer of Christendom
event.text: The cross flies over the Hagia Sophia. Constantinople (the city of Constantine, the Second Rome, the prize that eluded every Crusade) has been restored to Christian hands by Romanian arms. What the Fourth Crusade destroyed and the Ottomans claimed, Romania has reclaimed. The significance reverberates across Christendom and the Islamic world alike. A Romanian garrison holds the Theodosian Walls. Romanian ships control the Bosphorus. The question now is what Romania will do with this awesome inheritance.

options.text: Proclaim a new Rome under Romanian protection.

modifiers.name: A New Rome
modifiers.text: Romania proclaims itself protector of the Christian East, building a new imperial order with Constantinople as its spiritual center and Bucharest as its political heart.

options.text: The crusade does not end: it never will.

modifiers.name: Eternal Crusade
modifiers.text: Romania commits to perpetual holy war, maintaining networks of spies and mercenaries to sustain an endless campaign against the enemies of Christendom.

destiny.name: Black Sea Gateway
destiny.text: The port of Constanta and the Dobruja coast are the key to Romania's commercial future. Control the Black Sea gateway and the grain wealth of the Danubian plain will flow to every market in the Mediterranean.

event.title: Black Sea Gateway
event.text: The port of Constanta and the windswept coast of Dobruja are now Romanian. Where once the Genoese and Venetians competed for Black Sea trading privileges and the Ottomans controlled all maritime access, Romanian merchants now load grain, salt, and wool onto ships bound for every corner of the Mediterranean. The ancient Greek colony of Tomis, where Ovid spent his exile, has been reborn as Romania's window to the sea. The wealth of the Danubian plain no longer flows only to Ottoman or Habsburg markets. It flows where Romania directs it.

destiny.name: Breadbasket of Three Empires
destiny.text: Romania must expand its Danubian trade network by securing Ruse, the great crossing-point on the lower Danube, and by building up Braila, the port where the grain of the Wallachian plain is loaded for the sea.

conditions.text: We own Braila and its development is at least 11

event.title: Breadbasket of Three Empires
event.text: With Ruse secured and the lower Danube firmly under Romanian control, the agricultural heartland of the principalities has become the granary that feeds three empires. Romanian wheat flows downriver to the Black Sea and across the Mediterranean. Salt from the Carpathian mines travels to markets that once relied on distant suppliers. The boyar estates and peasant farms of Wallachia produce surpluses that fuel a growing commercial class in Bucharest and the Danubian river towns, and the quays of Braila are lined with grain ships. Romania is prosperous, but prosperity attracts attention.

options.text: Sell to everyone: let surplus be our weapon.

modifiers.name: Export Surplus
modifiers.text: Romanian grain, salt, and livestock flood the markets of southeastern Europe, enriching the kingdom's merchants even as prosperity breeds a certain complacency.

options.text: Build roads, bridges, and warehouses first.

modifiers.name: Invest in Infrastructure
modifiers.text: Rather than exporting raw commodities, Romania invests in roads, bridges, and administrative reform to integrate its diverse territories into a cohesive economic whole.

destiny.name: Paris of the Balkans
destiny.text: With Varna and the Black Sea coast under Romanian control, Bucharest can be built up into a cosmopolitan capital to rival any in Europe, the Micul Paris of the East.

conditions.text: We own Bucharest and its development is at least 40

event.title: Paris of the Balkans
event.text: Varna has joined Romania's Black Sea coastline, and Bucharest has been transformed. The city that was once a muddy Wallachian market town is now a capital of boulevards, academies, and diplomatic salons. French architects have designed its public buildings. Romanian intellectuals debate in coffeehouses that would not be out of place on the Left Bank. Foreign ambassadors jostle for influence at the royal court. 'Micul Paris', Little Paris, the Europeans call it, and for once the flattery is not entirely empty. The question is how to use this new stature.

options.text: Open our doors to the world.

modifiers.name: Cosmopolitan Capital
modifiers.text: Bucharest becomes a center of diplomacy and culture, attracting foreign envoys, merchants, and intellectuals to the court of the Romanian kingdom.

options.text: Command the Black Sea trade routes.

modifiers.name: Master of the Black Sea
modifiers.text: Romania builds a commercial fleet to dominate the Black Sea trade lanes, protecting its grain convoys and establishing itself as the maritime power of the western Black Sea.

units.name: Viteji
units.text: Elite courtier-cavalry of the Romanian principalities. The Viteji were minor nobles with permanent military obligations, fast, skilled horsemen who excelled at raiding and ambush in the Carpathian passes.

units.name: Viteji
units.text: Noble cavalry levied from the boyar estates of the principalities.

units.name: Lefegii
units.text: Professional mercenary infantry of the Romanian principalities. Experienced border troops skilled in mountain warfare, fortification defense, and skirmishing in difficult terrain.

units.name: Calarasi
units.text: Wallachian frontier cavalry, mounted scouts and patrol riders who guarded the borders of the principalities, carrying dispatches and raiding enemy supply lines.

units.name: Seimeni
units.text: Professional standing infantry of the Romanian principalities. Paid in cash and land grants, the Seimeni formed a disciplined core of guards loyal to the voivode rather than to the boyar council.

units.name: Rosiori
units.text: Romania's elite light cavalry, the Rosiori, 'Red Ones', served as reconnaissance, raiders, and pursuit troops. Distinguished by their red uniforms and superb horsemanship.

units.name: Dorobanti
units.text: The backbone of the modern Romanian army. Dorobanti were territorial infantry drawn from peasant communities across the kingdom, who proved their worth at Plevna and Grivitsa during the War of Independence.

units.name: Dorobanti
units.text: Territorial infantry levied from Romanian peasant communities.

units.name: Vanatori de Munte
units.text: Romanian mountain hunters, light infantry specialists trained in alpine warfare, expert at ambush and independent operations in the Carpathian highlands.

units.name: Panduri
units.text: Balkan irregular guerrilla fighters from the mountains of Oltenia. The Panduri specialized in ambush, raids, and scorched-earth tactics against Ottoman invaders.

buildings.name: Curtea Domneasca
buildings.text: The Princely Court, seat of voivodal authority where boyars gather to advise the prince, administer justice, and coordinate the governance of the realm.

buildings.name: Mountain Fortress
buildings.text: A Carpathian mountain fortress guarding the passes between the principalities, forming the backbone of Romanian defense against Ottoman, Hungarian, and Tatar invaders.

buildings.name: Fortified Church
buildings.text: A uniquely Transylvanian institution, churches built with defensive walls, towers, and granaries to shelter entire communities during raids.

buildings.name: Salt Works
buildings.text: Romanian salt mines at Praid, Turda, and Slanic have been worked since antiquity. Salt was so valuable that it served as currency and funded princely treasuries for centuries.

where.text: Salt is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Han Comercial
buildings.text: A Danubian trading inn where merchants, drovers, and river traders rest and exchange goods, the commercial nodes of Romanian trade networks.

buildings.name: Vie Domneasca
buildings.text: A princely vineyard on wine land, worked by the labour dues of the villages around it. The voivodes kept such vineyards at Dealu Mare, Odobesti and Cotnari, whose wine went north to the Polish court, and every harvest from them was larger for the care the prince's men gave the vines.

where.text: The location's raw material is Wine

buildings.name: Romanian School
buildings.text: An institution of Romanian-language education, established during the national awakening to teach in the mother tongue and forge a literate, nationally conscious citizenry.

buildings.name: Stana
buildings.text: A highland sheepfold and pastoral station. Romanian shepherds have driven their flocks across the Carpathian passes since time immemorial, producing wool, cheese, and hides for trade.

where.text: Wool is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Military Camp
buildings.text: A professional garrison and training facility for the reformed Romanian army, replacing the ad hoc feudal musters of the medieval Host.

buildings.name: Oil Refinery
buildings.text: An early petroleum refinery processing Romania's abundant crude oil. The Ploiesti refineries were among the first in the world, making Romania a pioneer of the petroleum age.

buildings.name: Leather Tannery
buildings.text: A tanning workshop processing the hides of the vast Romanian livestock herds into leather goods for domestic use and Danubian export.

buildings.name: Citadela Crestina
buildings.text: A grand Christian citadel, the fortress-cathedral that embodies Romania's role as the shield of Christendom, garrisoned by the kingdom's finest soldiers and blessed by the Orthodox Patriarch.

buildings.name: Bursa Comerciala
buildings.text: A grand commercial exchange where Danubian grain merchants, Black Sea traders, and Transylvanian mining agents converge to buy, sell, and finance the commerce of southeastern Europe.

list.name: Sfatul Domnesc
list.text: The Princely Council of the great boyars, attested in Wallachia from Basarab I and in Moldavia from Bogdan I. The marele logofat, vornic, vistier, spatar and postelnic register every charter the voivode signs; the dynasty rules only with their consent. At full investment the council binds the great families to the throne; neglected, it fractures into the rival boyar parties (Craiovesti, Movilesti) that depose princes from below.

list.name: Mitropolia
list.text: The two Romanian metropolitan sees: Ungro-Wallachia confirmed by Constantinople in 1359 under Iachint of Vicina, Moldavia raised to metropolitan status in 1401 under Iosif. The metropolitans crown each prince, register the realm's saints, and tie the principalities into the Athonite-Greek world through stavropegial monasteries (Tismana, Putna, Curtea de Arges, Neamt). When their dedicated monasteries lapse, revenue is siphoned away to Athos, Sinai and Jerusalem.

list.name: Pravila Mare
list.text: The Indreptarea legii printed at Targoviste in 1652 under Matei Basarab, drawing on the Byzantine basilika and the patriarchal canons; in Moldavia Vasile Lupu's Carte romaneasca de invatatura (Iasi, 1646) had already done the same work. For the first time the law of inheritance, dowry, criminal procedure and ecclesiastical jurisdiction was set into Romanian and printed in cyrillic on the prince's presses, taught in the monastic schools, and read from the burgher courts' benches.

list.name: Phanariote Administration
list.text: Between 1711 (Moldavia) and 1716 (Wallachia) and the Greek Revolution of 1821, the Porte leased both thrones to Constantinopolitan Phanariot families: the Mavrocordat, Ghica, Ypsilanti, Sutu, Caradja and Callimachi. Two-year contracts paid for by mucarrer fees forced the princes to recoup their costs through tax-farming. They Grecized the chancery, professionalised the divan into ministerial despartiri, abolished serfdom (1746/1749), and planted Greek schools at Bucharest and Iasi, but the high boyars hated them as foreigners and the peasantry was squeezed for the contract.

list.name: Asezamintul lui Mavrocordat
list.text: Constantin Mavrocordat held each throne six times between 1730 and 1769 and used those tenures to push through the Romanian enlightenment fiscal reform: the rusumat (a fixed quarterly head-tax replacing arbitrary cisla apportionments), a rebuilt cadastral catastif, the abolition of personal servitude (rumania abolished in Wallachia 5 August 1746; vecinia in Moldavia 6 April 1749), and the conversion of the boyar from domanial lord into a salaried state functionary.

list.name: Regulamentul Organic
list.text: Drafted by mixed boyar commissions at Bucharest and Iasi under the Russian governor-general Pavel Kiselyov, promulgated in Wallachia on 1 July 1831 and Moldavia on 1 January 1832. The two near-identical quasi-constitutions established a single elected General Assembly per principality, a state budget, separation of judicial and executive functions, ministries (interior, finance, justice, foreign affairs, war), a uniform corvee schedule of 12 days, and abolition of customs barriers between Wallachia and Moldavia: the institutional armature that permitted the 1859 union.
